title: Strict logarithmic base change and the saturated blowup Cartesian square
statement:
Let $g:(W,L)\to(V,N)$ be a strict morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] [def-per-strict-log-morphism]. Suppose $N$ is associated to a Zariski log structure. Then $L$ is associated to one as well, and the canonical morphism $g^{-1}\overline N\to\overline L$ on Zariski sites is an isomorphism, where the bars denote quotient by the respective sheaves of units. Let $K\subset\overline N$ be an ideal locally generated by finitely many, at least one, sections, and put $\mathcal I=\pi_N^{-1}K$, where $\pi_N:N\to\overline N$ is the quotient. Then $\mathcal I$ is a nonempty coherent log ideal, and the inverse image in $L$ of the ideal generated by $g^{-1}K$ in $\overline L$ is exactly $\mathcal I_W=(g^{-1}\mathcal I)L$.
For every nonempty coherent log ideal $\mathcal H\subset N$, both saturated log blowups $V'=\operatorname{LogBl}^{\mathrm{sat}}_{\mathcal H}V$ and $W'=\operatorname{LogBl}^{\mathrm{sat}}_{(g^{-1}\mathcal H)L}W$ exist, and there is a unique morphism $g':W'\to V'$ over $g$. It is strict, and its square with $W\to V$ is Cartesian in the fs category: for every fs log scheme $T$ with maps to $W$ and $V'$ agreeing in $V$, there is exactly one compatible map $T\to W'$. These maps agree with the specified morphism $g$ on the base, including its log-section maps, and their canonical identifications respect identity strict morphisms and composition.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11, pp.107--108: strict chart pullback, saturated universal property, and Cartesian compatibility in the fs category.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-zariski-fs-monoid-chart], cover $V$ by Zariski opens $U$ with fs charts $P\to N(U)$. On $g^{-1}U$ pull this chart back using the actual section maps of $g$. The mapping bijection in [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening] says that its associated log structure represents compatible maps from this prelog chart on the new base. Strictness [def-per-strict-log-morphism] says the same for $L|_{g^{-1}U}$. The mutually inverse maps supplied by these identical mapping properties fix $P$ and the new units; hence the pulled-back chart is a chart for $L$, with its specified map from $N$. Apply [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] to this chart. It is associated to a Zariski log structure. These local structures glue: on overlaps they are the associated Zariski log structures of the inverse image of the given Zariski structure on $V$; the identifications fix its prelog sections and units, so their compositions agree. Thus $L$ is Zariski.

source.place: VIII 3.3.4(ii), 3.3.8; associated-log mapping argument expands the same-chart assertion of 3.3.8.

proof.text: Let $w\in W$ and $v=g(w)$, in the preceding chart. Set $E_v=\{p\in P:\alpha(p)\in\mathcal O_{V,v}^{\times}\}$ and define $E_w$ using the pulled-back functions. The local ring homomorphism $\mathcal O_{V,v}\to\mathcal O_{W,w}$ preserves units and sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal, so $E_w=E_v$. By [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan], both characteristic stalks are $P_{E_v}/E_v^{\mathrm{gp}}$, and the map induced by $g$ is the identity on these representatives. Therefore $g^{-1}\overline N\to\overline L$ is an isomorphism of Zariski sheaves: its stalk maps are these bijections, and local inverse germs glue uniquely. This is the canonical map, not an abstract choice of isomorphism.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8 (same chart under strict pullback), with the characteristic formula of 3.3.12.

proof.text: Locally write $K=(k_1,\ldots,k_r)$ with $r\geq1$. In the quotient sheaf $N/\mathcal O_V^{\times}$, each $k_i$ lifts after an open refinement to $n_i\in N$. The inverse image of $K$ is exactly $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)N$: a section in that inverse image has characteristic $k_i+q$ locally, lift $q$, and its lift differs from $n_i$ times that lift only by a unit. This proves both inclusions. On an etale monoid chart every $n_i$ is locally a chart element times a unit by the chart pushout formula of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; refine for the finitely many $i$. Thus this ideal is nonempty coherent. On $W$ the ideal generated by $g^{-1}K$ has characteristic generators $\overline{g(n_i)}$ by step 2. The identical quotient argument says its inverse image is $(g(n_i))L=(g^{-1}\mathcal I)L$. These local equalities prove the required sheaf equality.

For the arbitrary nonempty coherent $\mathcal H$, pull a finite nonempty set of its chart generators through the strict map $g$. The chart argument of step 1, applied to these etale charts of $N$ with the mapping bijection of [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening], gives the same charts of $L$ and shows that $\mathcal H_W=(g^{-1}\mathcal H)L$ is nonempty coherent. Apply [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction] to $(V,N,\mathcal H)$ and $(W,L,\mathcal H_W)$ to obtain the saturated blowups $b_V:V^\prime\to V$ and $b_W:W^\prime\to W$. They have the fs universal property of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The chart lifting criterion [lem-trf-log-ideal-chart-lifting-criterion] applies even to fs test schemes not locally Noetherian, so no such restriction is imposed on the tests below. The pullback of $\mathcal H$ along $g b_W$ is exactly $b_W^*\mathcal H_W$, since both ideals are generated locally by the same images of sections of $\mathcal H$. It is principal. The universal property of $V^\prime$ gives exactly one $g^\prime:W^\prime\to V^\prime$ over the specified composite $g b_W$, including its log-section maps.

Let an fs log scheme $T$ have maps $a:T\to W$ and $d:T\to V^\prime$ with $ga=b_Vd$ as log morphisms. Pulling the principal ideal $b_V^*\mathcal H$ through $d$ keeps it principal: the image of any local generator is a local generator. This ideal is $a^*\mathcal H_W$ by equality of the composites on sections. The universal property [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives a unique $u:T\to W^\prime$ over $W$. The maps $g^\prime u$ and $d$ are both lifts of $ga$ to $V^\prime$, so that same universal property gives $g^\prime u=d$. Any compatible map must equal $u$ because it is a lift over $W$. This proves precisely the fs Cartesian universal property, on maps of log schemes.

source.place: VIII 3.3.10--3.3.11; two applications of the saturated universal property.

proof.text: To verify strictness, work etale locally on $V$ with an affine ideal chart $P\to A$ and nonempty finite generators $E\subset P$ of $\mathcal H$, and on affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of its pullback to $W$. Strictness gives the same $P$-chart on this pullback, with its specified ring map $A\to B$. By [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], the saturated blowups have charts indexed by $e\in E$ with monoid $R_e=\langle P,h-e\ (h\in E)\rangle^{\mathrm{sat}}\subset P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. The affine-atlas base-change assertion of [lem-trf-log-ideal-affine-atlas-gluing] identifies the charts and overlaps over $B$ with those over $A$ pulled back as schemes with pulled-back log structures. On each chart the map fixes $R_e$ and uses $A\to B$ on the coefficients. Its source log structure is therefore the associated inverse-image log structure, by the chart mapping bijection [lem-sfb-fine-chart-logification-thickening]. These maps are strict and agree on the localization overlaps. They equal $g^\prime$ by its uniqueness in step 4. The chart covers therefore show that $g^\prime$ is strict everywhere.

source.place: VIII 3.3.8--3.3.11: strict compatibility via the common fraction charts, also after saturation.

proof.text: For an identity strict morphism the induced map of blowups is the identity: both are lifts of the same base map, unique by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For composable strict maps, the composite of the constructed blowup maps and the map constructed for the composite are lifts of the same composite log morphism, so are equal by that universal property. Pullback ideals compose because either order generates the ideal by exactly the images of the original sections. Hence the resulting Cartesian identifications respect identities and composition; all equations are equations of log morphisms, including the section maps, rather than only equations of scheme maps.

source.place: VIII 3.3.9--3.3.10, pullbacks and pullbacks of towers; uniqueness gives coherence.

proof_origin.place: Expose VIII 3.3.4(ii),3.3.7--3.3.13, pp.107--109; chart and universal-property arguments expanded.
